plan.contextChunk: This figure contains five panels (a–e), each depicting a different normalization method using a 3D cube diagram with three labeled axes: position (spatial dimensions), batch index, and channel. Within each cube, orange-shaded regions indicate the set of activations that are jointly normalized together (i.e., the cells over which mean and variance statistics are computed), while gray regions indicate un-normalized cells. Panel (a) shows BatchNorm, where one horizontal slab spanning all batch instances and all spatial positions within a single channel is highlighted, reflecting normalization across the batch and spatial dimensions per channel. Panel (b) shows GhostNorm, where a region covering all batch instances and all channels but not spatial position is highlighted. Panel (c) shows LayerNorm, where all channels and spatial positions within a single batch instance are highlighted, reflecting per-sample normalization across all features. Panel (d) shows GroupNorm, where a subset of channels at all spatial positions within one batch instance is highlighted, reflecting normalization over a fixed group of channels per sample. Panel (e) shows InstanceNorm, where all spatial positions for a single channel within a single batch instance are highlighted, reflecting per-channel per-sample spatial normalization. This figure introduces and contrasts the major normalization strategies used in deep networks, illustrating how they differ in which axes they aggregate statistics over.

elements: single 3D activation cube shown one panel at a time, built from ~6 (batch index) × 6 (position) × 6 (channel) small voxels with visible grid edges
orange-highlighted voxels forming the normalization region for the currently selected method
gray un-highlighted voxels (excluded from the statistic)
axis label 'position' along the vertical/depth spatial axis
axis label 'batch index' along the horizontal receding axis
axis label 'channel' along the other receding axis
panel label beneath the cube naming the method (BatchNorm / GhostNorm / LayerNorm / GroupNorm / InstanceNorm)
during aggregation animation: a translucent moving scan layer sweeping through the orange region and a small readout showing running mean/variance being pooled

interactions.label: Normalization type
interactions.teaches: Switching methods reveals how each pools statistics over different axes: BatchNorm over batch+position per channel, GhostNorm over a restricted batch subgroup, LayerNorm over all channels+positions within one sample, GroupNorm over a channel subgroup within one sample, InstanceNorm over positions for one channel of one sample

interactions.label: Animate statistic aggregation
interactions.teaches: Watching the scan sweep the orange region makes concrete which axes (position, batch index, channel, or a channel subset) are collapsed into one shared mean and variance before normalizing those activations
Hovering a voxel reveals whether it belongs to the shared statistic group and its (batch, position, channel) coordinates, clarifying the inclusion boundary without labeling every cell
Rotating the cube shows the 3D extent of the highlighted region — e.g. that BatchNorm's slab runs through the whole batch and all positions but only one channel

demo_steps.title: BatchNorm
demo_steps.narration: One orange slab spans all batch indices and all positions within a single channel: statistics are pooled per channel across the batch and spatial dims.

demo_steps.title: LayerNorm
demo_steps.narration: The orange block covers all channels and all positions for one batch index — each sample is normalized over all its features, independent of the batch.

demo_steps.title: GroupNorm
demo_steps.narration: Only a subset of channels within one sample glows: GroupNorm pools over a fixed channel group and positions, bridging LayerNorm and InstanceNorm.

demo_steps.title: InstanceNorm
demo_steps.narration: A single orange column spans all positions for one channel of one sample — the smallest statistic group, per-sample per-channel.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: One cube at a time (panels a–e are NOT shown simultaneously; the normType toggle swaps them). Cube = 6×6×6 voxels, each voxel ~0.5 units, total cube ~3×3×3 world units centered at origin. Orientation as in source: +X (screen-right, receding slightly) carries batch index (front face visible), +Y vertical carries position, +Z receding diagonal carries channel (left face labeled 'channel', top face visible). Voxel fill colors: gray #b8c4c8 with dark edge lines #4a4a4a; highlight orange #d97a4e with darker orange face shading on the right faces (#a85a35 as in source). Highlight regions per method (indices 0-based): BatchNorm — all batch (0..5) × all positions (0..5) × channel=2 only, i.e. a slab one channel thick; GhostNorm — like BatchNorm slab but restricted to a contiguous batch subgroup (batch 2..5) so part of the slab is pale/washed orange; LayerNorm — batch=0..2 face slab spanning all channels × all positions (a vertical wall on the channel/batch side, matches panel c's left face); GroupNorm — channels 1..2 × all positions × batch=2 (a narrow two-channel column within one sample); InstanceNorm — channel=2 × batch=3 × all positions (a single 1×1 column of 6 voxels). Panel label text beneath the cube at y≈-2.2.
interactionPlan.notes: Build voxels as a single InstancedMesh of 216 boxes with per-instance color for cheap highlight switching; keep all five region definitions as index masks and recolor on toggle. Aggregation animation: step a translucent plane through the orange voxels along the dominant pooled axis, brightening each visited orange voxel and updating a mean/var counter overlay. Match source isometric pose: top, front (batch index face), and left (channel face) visible.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Select a normalization type: click BatchNorm, GhostNorm, LayerNorm, GroupNorm, or InstanceNorm to highlight the orange cells that share one mean and variance estimate, while gray cells remain excluded from the statistic
- Animate statistic aggregation: sweep across the highlighted region in the selected cube and show which axes are being pooled over — position, batch index, channel, or a subset of channels — before applying normalization to those activations
- Compare normalization scopes: toggle between the five panels to see how BatchNorm pools across batch and position per channel, GhostNorm uses a restricted batch grouping, LayerNorm pools all features within one sample, GroupNorm pools a channel group within one sample, and InstanceNorm pools spatial positions for one channel within one sample

discrepancies: LayerNorm highlights three batch samples (x<=2, half the cube) instead of a single sample slab spanning all channels and positions as in panel c

Source panels show the orange region as a thin slab/slice on the cube's front face; the generated BatchNorm highlight appears as a deep interior column band that reads differently from the source's flat face slice
Source shows all five panels side-by-side for comparison; the generated figure only shows one at a time (acceptable as a toggle, but side-by-side comparison is lost)
Panel letters a)–e) from the source are absent
evaluation.notes: Faithful voxel-cube normalization figure with an excellent five-way toggle, hover inspection, and aggregation animation; main flaw is LayerNorm pooling over three samples instead of one, misrepresenting that case.
action_items: Fix LayerNorm mask to a single batch sample (x === some index) spanning all channels and positions, matching panel c
Adjust BatchNorm highlight so the pooled slab reads as the flat batch×position slice for one channel as in panel a, clearly visible on the face
Add small panel-letter labels (a–e) or keep the norm name label consistent with the source's caption style

feedback.rationale: The plan and concept are sound (concept 4, interactivity 5), but the LayerNorm mask pools three samples instead of one and the BatchNorm slab reads as an interior column rather than a face slice — concrete geometry/label fixes the generator can apply without replanning.

Axis labels (position, channel, batch index) float near the cube corners rather than being aligned along the cube edges as in the source

evaluation.notes: All five normalization regions are correctly implemented with proper axis semantics, a useful aggregation animation, and hover inspection; main losses are the one-at-a-time presentation versus the source's five-panel layout and loosely placed axis labels.
action_items: Align the 'position', 'channel', and 'batch index' labels along their respective cube edges to match the source annotation style
Make GhostNorm's pale excluded subgroup more visually distinct (stronger tint contrast)
Consider a 'show all five' overview mode so the figure can resemble the source's side-by-side comparison

feedback.rationale: No failure modes, all scores 4–5 with empty plan action items, and remaining discrepancies are minor polish (label alignment, tint contrast, optional overview mode) that don't warrant another iteration.
